target: For every prime p, field K of characteristic p, integer 0 ≤ λ < p, and admissible lattice M in the characteristic-zero irreducible sl(2,C)-module V(λ), prove M ⊗_Z K is irreducible as an L(K)-module, where L(K) is the Chevalley form (including characteristic 2).
definitions_used: Use the source-context definitions: x,y,h satisfy [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=-2y, [x,y]=h; V(λ) is the (λ+1)-dimensional characteristic-zero highest-weight module with highest vector v and xv=0, hv=λv.
The divided-power integral enveloping algebra U_Z is generated by x^(r)/r! and y^(r)/r!; an admissible lattice M is a full Z-lattice stable under U_Z.
L(K) acts through the reductions of x,y,h. Irreducibility means nonzero and having no proper nonzero K-linear submodule.
proof:
Put e_i=y^i v/i! for 0≤i≤λ. These form a C-basis. From [x,y]=h and [h,y]=-2y, induction gives x e_i=(λ-i+1)e_(i-1), y e_i=(i+1)e_(i+1), with out-of-range terms zero. Iterating these formulas gives, for divided powers X_r=x^r/r! and Y_r=y^r/r!, X_r e_i=binom(λ-i+r,r)e_(i-r) and Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r), again zero when the index is out of range. In particular all X_r,Y_r preserve the standard Z-lattice M0 with basis (e_0,…,e_λ).

Fix p and let R=Z_(p). Regard M_R=R⊗_Z M as a full R-lattice in V(λ), and M0_R similarly. Since M is U_Z-stable, M_R is stable under the image A_R of U_Z⊗R. In the standard basis, X_λ sends e_λ to e_0 and kills e_i for i<λ; Y_λ sends e_0 to e_λ and kills e_i for i>0. Thus P_λ=Y_λX_λ is the matrix unit E_λλ. For every i, X_(λ-i)P_λ=E_iλ: it sends e_λ to e_i and kills the other basis vectors. For every j, P_λY_(λ-j)=binom(λ,j)E_λj. Because λ<p, both λ! and binom(λ,j) are units in R. Consequently E_λj and then E_ij=E_iλE_λj belong to A_R for all i,j. (When λ=0 this says the identity matrix belongs to A_R.)

The lattice M_R is therefore stable under every standard matrix unit E_ij. Write vectors in the basis e_i. The coordinate ideals I_i={a∈Q : a e_i∈M_R} are fractional R-ideals: they are nonzero fractional ideals because M_R is a full lattice. Stability under E_ij implies I_j⊆I_i, and reversing i,j gives equality. Moreover, for any vector of M_R, its individual coordinates times their basis vectors belong to M_R by applying E_ii. It follows that M_R=⊕_i I_i e_i=I M0_R for one fractional ideal I of R. Since R is a discrete valuation ring, I=p^nR for some integer n. Hence M_R/pM_R, with its induced action, is isomorphic to M0_R/pM0_R. Localization and reduction identify this quotient with M⊗_Z F_p. Extending scalars from F_p to K identifies M⊗_Z K with the scalar extension of the standard reduced module.

It remains to prove that this standard module is irreducible, rather than infer it from distinct h-weights. In characteristic p, for r≤λ<p, r! is invertible, so X_r and Y_r are scalar multiples of compositions of the Lie operators x and y. The matrix-unit construction above uses only r≤λ and coefficients binom(λ,j) that are nonzero modulo p. It therefore constructs every E_ij as a K-linear combination of compositions of x and y on the reduced standard module, also when p=2. Any L(K)-submodule is stable under x,y and their compositions, hence under all E_ij. If it contains a nonzero vector with a nonzero i-th coordinate, applying E_ji gives a nonzero multiple of e_j for each j; applying matrix units then yields every basis vector. Thus it is the whole module. The module has dimension λ+1 and is nonzero. For λ=0 it is one-dimensional and the same conclusion holds directly. This proves the target for every stated M, p, and K.
boundary_cases: λ=0 gives a one-dimensional trivial module. Characteristic 2 is included: the proof uses no distinction of h-weights, and all required factorials and binomial coefficients are units modulo p because λ<p. The arbitrary admissible lattice is handled by localization and the matrix-unit argument; it is not assumed to be the standard lattice.
